highlights.title: Why North Korea's 'elite' hackers are the prime suspect in major Binance hack
highlights.summary: If the accusations are true, the record-making heist shows how powerful suspected North Korean hackers have become.
body: Two major blockchain analytics firms say they have robust intelligence pointing to a North Korean state-backed group as the likely culprits in the $6.3bn (£4.7bn) hack of Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange.
The Lazarus Group, a North Korean hacking unit also known as TraderTraitor, was identified "with high confidence" by TRM Labs, as well as Chainalysis.
This incident is just the latest linked to the country, one of the poorest in the world and where access to the internet is severely restricted.
Experts accuse the government of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un of relying on cybercrime to finance itself, something Pyongyang has long denied.

highlights.title: Aston Villa to take legal action against Jamie Carragher for ‘unacceptable insults’
highlights.summary: Villa chair announces plan on social media. Carragher said club will ‘never be Man United’ Aston Villa have announced plans to take legal action against Jamie Carragher following his “unacceptable insults” about the club and its supporters.
body: Carragher told Villa fans to “shut the fuck up” after facing criticism for suggesting Unai Emery should consider taking the Manchester United job. Villa responded on Friday evening with a statement on X signed by their chair, Nassef Sawiris.

“Aston Villa will initiate legal action against Jamie Carragher for his unacceptable insults about the club and its fans,” the statement said. “Aston Villa will not allow anyone to stop our ascension in English and European football. Nassef Sawiris, chairman.”

Former Liverpool defender Carragher made his remarks on the Stick to Football podcast while discussing the prospect of Emery replacing Michael Carrick at Old Trafford. The 48-year-old Sky Sports pundit argued there was a hierarchy in football, saying “Aston Villa will never be Man United”.

“I’m not trying to annoy Villa fans but there is a chain in football, whether you like it or not,” said Carragher. “So Real Madrid will take Man United’s best player, they’ll take [Cristiano] Ronaldo. There’s very few above United, the same with Liverpool.

highlights.title: 15 Classic Games That Prove Gameplay Is More Important Than Graphics
highlights.summary: There’s no getting around it: graphics matter a great deal for video games. For many years, visual fidelity alone was one of the best reasons to invest in new consoles and better gaming PCs. There have always been games that didn’t compete for a position at the head of the pack, though.
body: As we look forward to the visual powerhouse that is Grand Theft Auto 6, here are 15 classic games that prove great graphics aren’t everything — and in many ways make the case that good gameplay is a more important factor for timelessness.

N+ is the console version of N, a game originally developed as an Adobe Flash game, but Metanet Software partnered with other developers to produce a version for Xbox Live Arcade. The game features extremely simple controls that allow players to run and leap around hundreds of stages in treacherous, mostly barren environments. It’s not a visual stunner, but the gameplay loop kept players coming back for dozens of hours.

Final Fantasy games have tended to push visual boundaries, one after another. Following on the heels of Final Fantasy 8, which featured realistic models for its memorable cast of characters, Final Fantasy 9 went in a different direction. Its chibi characters were expressive and the world beautiful, but in some respects it felt like a visual regression that Final Fantasy 10 rectified one year later. Even in a world with gorgeous stunners like Final Fantasy 16, this much older title remains a delight to play.

body: Whether it’s Pokémon Sleep turning towards nightmarish ghosts like Gengar, or a growing cast of horror characters in Fortnite, there’s a good chance one game or other will land a scare.

This year, Epic Games, Zynga, The Pokémon Company, Scopely, Intelligent Systems and even The New York Times are among those dressing up their games for the occasion. Many of them also recently landed among our Top 50 Mobile Game Makers of 2026.

The aptly named Fortnitemares event has brought a month of cursed content to Epic Games’ flagship, tapping into a lineup of characters like Freddy Krueger, Ghost Face and Freddy Fazbear. In fact, characters from the Five Nights at Freddy’s universe are going all-in on the fright factor, with their outfits able to show battle damage.

Other IPs trickling in throughout October have included Hollow Knight, Slender Man, Beetlejuice and Obsession. Meanwhile, gameplay has seen players firing pumpkin rockets, teleporting around and dropping into Reload’s Nitemare Island.

highlights.title: Once again, NASA is asking for ideas to rescue Hubble from certain death
highlights.summary: The Hubble Space Telescope still shines in the eyes of astronomers after 36 years in orbit, but it is not as nimble as it once was. Left alone, the observatory will plunge back into the atmosphere in the early-to-mid-2030s, closing the book on one of the most famous scientific instruments of the…
body: NASA last raised the orbit of Hubble in 2002, when the Space Shuttle Columbia visited the observatory for a servicing mission. The final shuttle servicing flight in 2009 did not reboost the telescope’s orbit, and with the retirement of the shuttle fleet two years later, Hubble has steadily lost altitude with no way to stave off eventual destruction.

The space agency released a Request For Information (RFI) on Thursday asking commercial companies for ideas on how to reboost, service, or a controlled disposal of Hubble. Responses are due November 30. Specifically, NASA is looking for information about companies’ current and near-term capabilities for capturing Hubble and boosting it to an altitude of at least 373 miles (600 km), enhancing the telescope’s performance through, or guiding Hubble to a controlled reentry.

“The requirement includes that the boost and/or servicing mission must not harm the HST and that this mission is expected to occur by 2032,” NASA wrote in the RFI. The contractor would be responsible for providing the launch vehicle, servicing spacecraft, mission operations, and “crew if applicable.”

highlights.title: The biggest names in AI are backing a new way to opt out of scraping
highlights.summary: OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, and Anthropic say they will adopt a new standard that publishers can use to opt out of being scraped by AI, as reported earlier by Search Engine Roundtable.
body: The new control will allow publishers to apply their AI training preferences across multiple crawlers.

The shared “policy token” signal is proposed by Kevin Kelley, a technical lead for standards at Anthropic, as part of the Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF). It will live within a website’s robots.txt file, which has long signaled which web crawlers can and can’t scrape a site — whether for search indexing, archiving, or AI training. Currently, sites have to signal their AI training preferences separately to each AI company.

The announcement comes as publishers grapple with the continuing influx of AI crawlers scraping their sites and feeding their content into AI models. Some companies and organizations have attempted to combat unauthorized scraping, with the Really Simple Licensing (RSL) standard giving publishers the ability to charge crawlers that visit their sites, and Cloudflare blocking AI crawlers by default.

highlights.title: Top 10 Pokémon Cards Most Likely to Be Fake
highlights.summary: The more Pokémon trading cards pop off, the more potential players and collectors have to worry about one thing: counterfeit cards. Sometimes, a fake card will be obvious. As more money pours into the hobby, however, there's more incentive than ever to pull a fast one on people.
body: Grading service PSA recently published a fraud report that goes over trends in forged and altered collectibles, including Pokémon cards. As PSA is in the business of assessing card conditions and determining their value, the service needs to be good at spotting counterfeits. According to the report, 2025 saw an incredible 407% increase in altered Pokémon cards attempting to be graded.

The specific characters that swindlers target likely won't be a surprise, but it's still worth knowing which cards should warrant a second look IRL. It's easy to assume only the most expensive and elusive cards on the market would be in contention, but that's not the case. The top card can be purchased for $150 or under. It makes sense, though: It's harder to pass off an ultra-rare card as legitimate. It's also difficult to sell a card that's the equivalent to a down payment on a house.

body: Well, Maher took the stage of “Real Time” Friday night and, before welcoming Ted Cruz and the aforementioned Kid Rock as guests, wasted no time addressing that incredibly long Trump rant.

“Did you see the 1,300-word [Truth Social post] he sent out? Longest ever! Kind of a flex,” offered Maher during his monologue. “I tell ya, dining at the White House is the opposite of the Cheesecake Factory — after you leave, they review you!”

“He went off on me like Kelly Clarkson in a toy store,” he continued. “Eating with Trump is like dating Taylor Swift: It’s a lot of laughs at the time, but later on, they’re tearing you a new asshole.”

Maher wasn’t finished: “Look, I don’t want it to be this way. The whole point of having these dinners was talk, disagree but listen — which he does, in person — but don’t hate each other, I go back to my job here and the heartaches begin. I’m not going to refute everything, but I do have to address a few of the allegations.”

highlights.title: MIT affiliates named 2026 Schmidt Sciences AI2050 Fellows
highlights.summary: Five MIT faculty members and two additional alumni are honored with fellowships to advance research on beneficial AI.
body: Five MIT faculty members and two additional alumni were recently named to the 2026 cohort of AI2050 Fellows. The honor is announced annually by Schmidt Sciences, Eric and Wendy Schmidt’s philanthropic initiative that aims to accelerate scientific innovation.

Conceived and co-chaired by Eric Schmidt and James Manyika, AI2050 is a philanthropic initiative aimed at helping to solve hard problems in artificial intelligence. Within their research, each fellow will contend with the central motivating question of AI2050: “It’s 2050. AI has turned out to be hugely beneficial to society. What happened? What are the most important problems we solved and the opportunities and possibilities we realized to ensure this outcome?”
MIT alumni Irene Chen PhD '22 and Allison Z. Koenecke '14 as well as former postdoc Juan Carlos Perdomo were also named AI2050 Early Career Fellows.

highlights.title: Flesh-eating screwworms spread to third state and are attacking pets
highlights.summary: For a genuine fright this Halloween, you can turn your gaze to the southern border, where ravenous, flesh-eating maggots are festering and have taken to eating people's pets.
body: This week, the country’s New World Screwworm (NWS) infestation spread to a third state, Arizona, which joins New Mexico and Texas in being plagued by the horrifying parasites. To date, 74 animal cases have been identified in the US since the flies re-invaded the country in June.

The flies lay hundreds of eggs in wounds and moist orifices of animals, and the resulting voracious maggots feast on their victims. The maggots resemble screws and tortuously bore and twist into living flesh, causing severe, sometimes fatal wounds, before dropping to the ground to develop into adults.

Because of their ability to ravage livestock, the flies were eliminated from the country in the 1960s through aerial releases of sterile male flies, which thwart successful breeding. For years, they were held at bay using a biological barrier along the Darién Gap at the border of Panama and Colombia. But the barrier was breached in 2022, and the flies have made their way back to the US through Central America.

Nvidia is in talks to guarantee billions in debt financing for AI cloud provider Nscale’s planned Anthropic data center in West Virginia, The Information reported Thursday. Bloomberg later corroborated the report. Anthropic has signed a $44.6 billion contract for the project’s first building alone, according to Nscale’s IPO filing. In essence, the chipmaker would be co-signing a customer’s loans, a sign of how hard the AI industry is working to keep its buildout plans afloat as investors grow jittery about the amounts of money involved.

The proposed arrangement would help Nscale secure financing for the electricity and construction costs of its West Virginia campus. Under what’s known as a residual value guarantee, Nvidia would step in if Nscale defaulted on construction payments, temporarily take over the facility, and help find a buyer and new tenant, according to The Information.

highlights.title: England see off USA to return to winning ways
highlights.summary: England's Red Roses return to winning ways, but without entirely vanquishing doubts over their position at the top of the women's game, as they see off the United States.
body: England's Red Roses returned to winning ways, but without entirely vanquishing doubts over their position at the top of the women's game, as they saw off a spirited United States in New Jersey.
England started steadily enough with wing Claudia Moloney-MacDonald crossing twice in the first 12 minutes, her second coming via a looping mis-pass from fly-half Holly Aitchison.
However the United States, who were obliterated 69-7 in the opening match of England's march to the Rugby World Cup last year, stuck in the contest far longer than they did that day in Sunderland.
The sixth-ranked underdogs were still snarling deep into the second half with one thunderous hit from Alev Kelter, hoisting and dumping England captain Meg Jones, rallying her team.

highlights.title: Timbaland Files $15 Million Fraud Lawsuit Against Former Managers
highlights.summary: The super-producer alleges that former manager Gary Marella and business manager Bruce Seckendorf "used their entrusted authority to enrich themselves and others, conceal financial misconduct, and deplete Timbaland’s valuable assets."
body: Timbaland has filed a $15 million lawsuit against his former manager and business manager, accusing the two executives of fraud, breach of fiduciary duty and civil theft, among other claims.
The former business manager Bruce Seckendorf, Timbaland, whose real name is Timothy Mosley, alleges, “failed to pay Mosley’s mortgage and allowed his home to reach the brink of foreclosure.”

The suit claims Seckendorf’s firm “failed to timely pay substantial federal taxes, causing millions in penalties and interest, while continuing to pay themselves, the Marella Defendants, and other professionals millions in commissions, fees, and purported loan repayments.”

Per the suit, Timbaland only learned of the alleged misconduct because he got a foreclosure notice at his home last year. After receiving the notice, the suit says, Timbaland called Seckendorf, who the producer says failed to “clearly explain why his office had failed to make the mortgage payments without informing Mosley.”

highlights.title: Q&A: Hey AI, who should I vote for this year?
highlights.summary: MIT professors Adam Berinsky and Chara Podimata discuss a new project to track how AI chatbots are responding to questions about the 2026 U.S. midterm elections.
body: People are peppering artificial intelligence chatbots everyday with questions, but when it comes to politics and the looming 2026 U.S. midterm elections, what role are AI platforms playing? Could an AI chatbot sway a voter to switch parties or re-examine their political beliefs?

MIT researchers have built a new dashboard, called the LLM Election Observatory, to examine, in real-time, how popular AI chatbots are responding to questions about the 2026 midterm elections. The team behind the dashboard — led by Professor Adam Berinsky, Assistant Professor Chara Podimata, and Professor Charles Stewart III — has extensive experience studying voting and election administration, AI and misinformation, and how AI systems are impacting human decision making. In an effort to better understand how AI is shaping the election, they designed the dashboard to simulate how individuals across the country communicate with chatbots.

Kimi Antonelli, who only needs to finish ninth in Sunday's race to become Formula 1's youngest-ever world champion, was a tenth down on his team-mate Russell in fourth.
Hamilton had been on course to go fastest as the session approached its midway point before suffering what appeared to be an engine issue in the final sector of his push lap, leaving him 11th.

He completed the lap but was then swiftly told by his engineer to pull over on track, ending his session early and denying him valuable information that his rivals were able to gather with their race simulations.

highlights.summary: Also known as Easter Island, this Polynesian isle has long been an aspirational destination—here's how to visit.
body: Today, this Chilean territory is essentially an open-air archaeological museum, with many of its enigmatic moai (representations of Polynesian ancestors) returned to their upright positions following seven decades of restoration. Of course to see Rapa Nui only through its superhuman past is to miss much of the story: The island’s distinct Polynesian culture remains a vital presence, particularly in its sole town, Hanga Roa, where nights come alive with cheerful ukulele music and hip-swirling dances. There’s also a vast, vibrant sea, windswept volcanic plains, and a food culture that draws on the island’s rich heritage and maritime setting.
As a repeat visitor to the island, this is my guide to Rapa Nui.

highlights.title: ‘A Few Good Men’ Marked Its Broadway Opening With a Few Starry Friends
highlights.summary: Before it was an Oscar-nominated drama, “A Few Good Men” premiered on Broadway in 1989, helping to launch the career of its 20-something playwright, Aaron Sorkin. Now, nearly four decades later, the work has returned to the Main Stem, directed by six-time Tony Award winner Michael Arden.
body: The work—a thrilling study of military honor, institutional might, and a dauntless pursuit of the truth—is now brought to life by Tom Blyth, who makes his Broadway debut as Daniel Kaffee, the brash Navy lawyer portrayed by Cruise onscreen. Initially more interested in negotiating a convenient settlement than fighting for justice, Kaffee finds himself drawn into a trial involving two young Marines accused of killing a fellow serviceman after carrying out an illegal order. In so doing, he gets to know the darker side of the Corps.

For Blyth, who broke out on film in The Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes, the play pushed him into new territory. “I’m excited. My whole career so far has been about testing myself and trying to do things I’ve not done yet,” the Juilliard-trained British actor told Vogue on the red carpet. “To be totally transparent, the first couple of weeks were terrifying, but I’ve learned that if I mess up, I’ve got to keep going. Quite literally, the show must go on. It’s the most invigorating way to act, and it makes you a better screen actor as well. If you can do this, you’re infinitely better on screen.”
